summary: Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University, studied at the University of Tokyo, and studied under Akira Hirakawa. He served as professor of religious studies at the University of Virginia.

Paul Hacker was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin. He held the chair for Indology at the University of Bonn (1955–1963) and headed the Institute of Indian Studies at the University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, he held posts at Canterbury and Stanford University as professor of religious studies.
Paul Hoornaert is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts at Kanazawa University, attested in 1991 as lecturer and in 2002.

Paul Hoswell Hardacre was a historian who studied at Stanford University (~1933–1937) and the University of California, Los Angeles (~1938–1941). He served as a historian of Stuart England at Vanderbilt University from circa 1947 to 1980.

Paul J. Griffiths is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Oxford and Wisconsin under Minoru Kiyota, he held professorships at the University of Chicago, University of Illinois Chicago, and Duke University (2007–2017).
Paul Kingsbury is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).

Paul Kiparsky is a linguist and Indologist who studied at King Edward's School and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology under Morris Halle (~1962–1965). He joined the faculty at Stanford University circa 1984.

Paul L. Swanson is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He served as a professor at Nanzan University and directed the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (attested 1999–2009).

Paul Mendes-Flohr was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and history. He studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University, directed at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006), and served as professor of modern Jewish history and thought at the University of Chicago.

Paul Mus was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history. Educated at Oxford, EPHE, INALCO, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot, he held professorships at EPHE, Collège de France (1946), and Yale University (1951).
Paul Nietupski is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).
Paul Passy was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1881–1887). He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1894 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Sorbonne and INALCO under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes, holding posts at the EFEO and the Collège de France (1909–1945).

Paul Regnaud was an Indologist and linguist who studied as an élève at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1870–1876). He subsequently held a post at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur was a philosopher who studied at the University of Rennes and the University of Paris. He held faculty posts at the University of Strasbourg, Paris Nanterre University, Université catholique de Louvain, and the University of Chicago (1970–1985).

Paul Tedesco was a linguist, Iranist, and Indologist who studied philology at the University of Vienna (1916–1921). He held research posts at Princeton (~1944–1952) and served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Yale University (1952–1966).

Paul Thieme was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorships at the University of Halle (1941–1953), Yale University (1954–1960), and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and theologian who earned degrees from Breslau and Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at TU Dresden, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard University (1955–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (~1970–1976). He served as associate professor of Chinese and department chair at the University of Colorado from circa 1985 to 1993.
